title: Peer identity and authenticated handshake
summary: Peer authentication uses the configured transport PSK to authenticate HELLO and CHALLENGE with HMAC-SHA-512. Source IP is an admission fact, not an identity credential; the authenticated transcript binds queue-manager identities, receiver channel, principal, key id and both fresh nonces before protected commands are accepted.
invariants: Source IP is not a credential; cryptographic peer proof is still mandatory.
HELLO identifies source manager, destination manager, receiver channel, principal and key id.
Server challenge is authenticated before the client considers the session established.
keyId selects/identifies key material; it does not itself grant authority.

provenance.claim: HELLO and CHALLENGE authentication and the distinction between IP admission and identity.
Protocol text binds protocol identity, managers, channel, principal, key id and nonces.
Client verifies authenticated server challenge before constructing session crypto.
